questions.prompt: What money is used in Luxembourg?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Luxembourg is the euro.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Luxembourg is Luxembourg.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Luxembourg article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Luxembourg is Luxembourg.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Luxembourg on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Luxembourg on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Luxembourg?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Luxembourg article.

questions.proof: The main language is Luxembourgish but French and German is also spoken there.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Luxembourg about 2,593 square kilometres; Saint Lucia about 617 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres; Malta about 316 square kilometres.
